title: Trump Administration Prioritizes Affordability by Announcing Major Crackdown on Health Care Fraud
supports: CMS announced a $259,505,491 deferral of federal matching funds associated with Minnesota's Q4 FY2025 Medicaid spending while further review/investigation was completed.

CMS described $243.8 million of the deferral as related to unsupported or potentially fraudulent Medicaid claims and approximately $15.4 million as related to claims involving individuals lacking satisfactory immigration status.
CMS stated that a deferral is among federal financial-management tools available when state obligations are not met and tied the action to its broader Minnesota program-integrity review.

money.notes: Deferral is not final disallowance, adjudicated fraud loss, restitution, or money recovered.
Potentially fraudulent or unsupported is not the same as proven fraud.

does_not_support: The $259.5 million deferral is not a court finding that $259.5 million was stolen.

A deferred federal match can later be resolved through documentation, adjustment, disallowance, or other federal-state financial processes; the release does not establish the final disposition of every dollar.
The release is an agency position and financial-control action, not a criminal charging instrument against Minnesota officials.
